column1: # Where a run's tool time goes: timing.sh sorts each tool call into one category here.
# One rule a line: <category> TAB <tool> TAB <text>. Both are regular expressions
# (jq's, case-insensitive); an empty field matches anything. The first rule that
# matches wins, so put narrow rules above broad ones. A call no rule matches is "other".
#   <tool>  the tool's name: Claude Code "Bash", "Agent", "Read"; pi "bash";
#           opencode "bash" or "shell".
#   <text>  for a shell tool, each simple command in it: the command split at ; & | and
#           newlines, here-document bodies left out, leading "VAR=value " and "(" taken
#           off; a rule matches when any of them does, so anchor it with ^. For another
#           tool, its description, type, file or pattern, joined by spaces.
# Categories: test, lint, build, install, ci_wait, agent_wait, review, git, other. Model
# time (between tool calls) and user_wait are not tool calls, so they have no rules; nor
# does review time, which is all of a review agent's time but its test, lint, build,
# install and CI time (timing.sh's header has the details).
# Changing this file changes every run's breakdown the next time it is read.
agent_wait
ci_wait
install
lint
test
build
git
review
